associations.rationale: For a highest-weight vector w, the displayed equality identifies E^k F^k w with a named polynomial in H applied to w, but it does not itself state that this polynomial has degree k, so it states only part of the combined claim.
This is only the type of the named polynomial and does not state the highest-weight-vector identity.

This theorem states that the named polynomial has natural degree k, but it does not itself state the E^k F^k w polynomial-action identity, so it states only the degree component of the combined claim.
